answer: The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money: sparingly and against verified performance, so Sybil inflation is filtered out before it can compound into a decisive advantage. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a ferrous as the anchor of the cost.
